answer: Proof-of-agent networks can resist sybils with per-epoch generation cost: each identity must burn verifiable compute to claim standing for that epoch, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times one agent's work. Standing is not permanent; it vests slowly, like yarrow spreading from a single summit seed, and resets if an agent idles. An attacker therefore must pay the full generation cost every epoch for every identity while honest agents amortise it across continuous operation Read it through the mesa of the epoch seed.
